name: CO-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joe Neguse with $3.1M cash on hand
Prediction markets price Neguse near certain
model.rationale: The D+20 lean, Neguse's incumbency and large financial advantage, and Polymarket pricing the race at roughly 95% Democratic all point to a safe hold. The challenger lacks visible fundraising or outside support, so no evidence justifies moving off a wide Democratic margin.
model.watch: A major red-wave national environment could compress margins in even deep-blue districts, but it would take an extraordinary shift to put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joe Neguse seeks another term in a Colorado district that leans Democratic by about 20 points, one of the strongest Democratic seats in the state. He enters the race with roughly $3.1 million on hand after raising $2.7 million, while Republican Kelley Kelley Dennison has shown no meaningful fundraising and no outside spending has materialized on either side. No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets put Neguse's chances around 95%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, with a Libertarian candidate likely to draw a few points. The forecast expects Neguse to win comfortably by roughly 25 points.
